Scaling Event Pipelines to Trillions of Events

Every day our systems produce an enormous number of events. In this post we describe how the data platform team rebuilt the pipeline that moves those events from producers to the warehouse, the trade-offs we considered, and the lessons we learned while migrating hundreds of services without downtime.

Background

The original pipeline was built years ago around a single cluster. As traffic grew, partitions became hot, consumer lag increased and the on-call burden became unsustainable. We needed a design that could scale horizontally, isolate noisy tenants and give producers clear back-pressure signals.

The new architecture

We split the pipeline into regional ingestion tiers, a routing layer and per-domain sinks. Each tier can be scaled independently and failures are contained within a region.

  • Regional Kafka clusters with tiered storage
  • A stateless router written in Java
  • Flink jobs for enrichment
router.route(event).to(sink)

Read more in the Kafka documentation.

Results

Consumer lag dropped by ninety percent, costs fell by a third and the number of pages for the on-call engineer went from several a week to almost none. We hope these lessons are useful for your own systems.
